column4: This verse joins earth, sky, rain, and fruits brought forth for people; it is a direct formulation of the cloud nourishing the ground.
Water sent from the sky revives the earth after its death; this repeated rain-to-growth formulation fits the section's central scene.
Rain makes gardens of beauty grow where people could not grow their trees; it directly stages the source's rabāb cloud as plant nourishment.
The verse says rain grows every kind of noble plant; it states the same cloud-to-vegetation relation as the source's dictionary image.
Water sent from the sky produces fruits of varied colors; this is a specific continuation of the image of cloud, water, and growth.
Dead earth is made alive and yields grain for food; it directly parallels rain-supported growth as provision.
The next ayah names gardens of dates and grapes with springs; its contribution is a cultivated landscape where water and plant growth meet.
The verse pairs night and day, rain from the sky, winds, and life returned to dead earth; it gathers several features of this image in one sign.
Winds are sent as good news and let people taste God's mercy; this gives a specific wind-as-blessing parallel to the source's moist south-wind sense of niʿma.
The ayah asks whether people send drinking water down from the clouds or God does; 56:68 supplies the water being considered, while this ayah identifies the cloud as its source.
The verse says God could make the drinking water bitter; after the cloud-sourced water in 56:69, it marks the contingent boundary of water as provision.
After the rain-grown vegetation that dries in 18:45, this verse distinguishes the passing adornment of wealth and children from enduring good deeds, completing the passage's transience theme.
Addressing the Prophet, the verse says people would have dispersed if he had been harsh and hard-hearted; it gives a specific counterpoint to 93:10's command not to rebuke the asker.
The verse tells the hearer to repel evil with what is better; that concrete reversal illuminates the section's warning against answering a petitioner with harshness.
The verse says every living thing was made from water; the section's water-fed plant growth is one concrete instance of this broader water-to-life claim.
